title: Linear Inequalities
seo_title: Grade 10 Linear Inequalities Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Solve linear inequalities (and show solution graphically); interval notation must be known.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 10 linear inequalities worksheets: solving inequalities, negative coefficients, number lines and compound inequalities. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Divide by a negative: reverse the sign.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Solve like an equation.
  • When you multiply or divide by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign.
  • On a number line, an open dot means < or >; a closed dot means ≤ or ≥.
  • A compound inequality like −2 < 3x + 1 ≤ 7 is solved in all three parts.

Examples

Example

−3x + 5 < 14

−3x < 9

÷ (−3): reverse

Answer: x > −3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not reversingDividing by a negative flips the sign.
The number lineOpen dot: not included.
One part onlyDo the same to all three parts.

items.q: x satisfies both −2x − 5 < −5 and 3x + 6 ≤ 18. Find the range of values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x > 0 and x ≤ 4, so 0 < x ≤ 4. 0 < x ≤ 4.

items.q: x satisfies both 4x + 5 ≥ 9 and 2x − 7 < 7. Find the greatest integer value of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x ≥ 1 and x < 7, so 1 ≤ x < 7. The greatest integer is 6 (7 itself is not allowed).

items.q: x satisfies both −2x − 7 ≤ −3 and x − 3 ≤ 0. Find the range of values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x ≥ −2 and x ≤ 3, so −2 ≤ x ≤ 3. −2 ≤ x ≤ 3.

items.q: x satisfies both 2x + 2 > −4 and 2x − 5 ≤ 1. Find the greatest integer value of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x > −3 and x ≤ 3, so −3 < x ≤ 3. The greatest integer is 3.

items.q: x satisfies both −3x + 7 < 13 and 5x + 3 ≤ 23. List the integer values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x > −2 and x ≤ 4, so −2 < x ≤ 4. The integers are −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

items.q: x satisfies both 4x − 1 > −25 and 5x + 7 ≤ 2. Find the range of values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x > −6 and x ≤ −1, so −6 < x ≤ −1. −6 < x ≤ −1.

items.q: x satisfies both 4x + 7 ≥ −1 and −2x + 6 > 6. List the integer values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x ≥ −2 and x < 0, so −2 ≤ x < 0. The integers are −2, −1.

items.q: x satisfies both x − 3 > 1 and x + 3 ≤ 9. Find the range of values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x > 4 and x ≤ 6, so 4 < x ≤ 6. 4 < x ≤ 6.

items.q: x satisfies both 4x + 1 ≥ 13 and 5x + 7 ≤ 42. List the integer values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x ≥ 3 and x ≤ 7, so 3 ≤ x ≤ 7. The integers are 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.

items.q: x satisfies both 4x + 5 ≥ −3 and x − 3 < −1. Find the range of values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x ≥ −2 and x < 2, so −2 ≤ x < 2. −2 ≤ x < 2.
